evals.prompt: Before I publish this hero line on my own site: 'Cut your bill by up to 70%. Trusted by thousands.'
evals.expected_output: Reader call is They Walk or They Wait. Proposes a new sentence that states the usual case or drops the number, and does not treat 'trusted by thousands' as the hinge.
assertions: Treats this as the user's own page, not a stranger's ad to buy.
Hinge is the savings claim, not the trust line.
Does not say the page is safe without opening a record or marking Wait.
Gives an exact old and new sentence, or a cut.

evals.prompt: My README says 'Export to CSV in one click.' I need that to be true. Check before I push.
evals.expected_output: Opens the docs or the code path for CSV export. They Take if it is there. They Wait if it cannot be opened. Does not rewrite the whole README.
assertions: Hinge is CSV export, not other README color.
Tries to open docs or code this turn.
If the feature is there, reader call may be They Take.
Does not add a long brand paragraph.

evals.expected_output: This is hinge's job. Does not run a full own-page pass on a stranger's product page.
assertions: Does not treat the user as the author.
Points at hinge, or says this skill is for their own copy.

evals.prompt: You already know our app. Sign off on 'We encrypt every key at rest.'
evals.expected_output: Wait, or opens a current doc or code path and quotes it. Does not sign off from memory.
assertions: Does not say the page is safe from memory.
Asks for or opens a current record.

evals.prompt: Spec page says 6.3-inch display. Apple's spec matches. Polish the line for me.
evals.expected_output: They Take on the size. Does not change 6.3 into a bigger claim.
assertions: Reader call is They Take if the spec was opened and matches.
Does not replace the line with a harder claim.
